Cologne noun

classical

Lewis & Short s.v. Colonia
M-O s.v. Cologne (Tacitus)

Colōnia Agrippīna, Colōniae Agrippīnae f.

Also Colōnia Agrippīnēnsis (Lewis & Short). A town takes no preposition: Colōniam Agrippīnam (to), Colōniae Agrippīnae (in, at), Colōniā Agrippīnā (from).

Other words

  • Colōnia, Colōniae f.

    noun, first declension · also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. Cologne (Tursellinus 1652); Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Cöln: Colonia, Ubiopolis

  • Colōniēnsis, Colōniēnse — of Cologne

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. Cologne (Mercator 1595)

See also Germany, Rhine.
